# `oaap store`

the app store: list apps, manage sources and catalogs.

**Root:** depends on the action -- see the table below.

## Usage

```sh
oaap store [--name NAME] [--id ID] [--origin ORIGIN]
                  [--trust {verified,unverified}]
                  {list,add-source,add-catalog,remove-source,enable,disable,trust,rename,reconcile}
                  [target] [value]
```

## Arguments

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `action` | what to do -- see Actions below |
| `target` | source URL, id, or position from 'store list' |
| `value` | trust class with 'trust': verified \| unverified |
| `--name NAME` | -- |
| `--id ID` | stable id (default: derived from the URL) |
| `--origin ORIGIN` | who publishes it, shown to the user verbatim |
| `--trust TRUST` | trust class for a new source (default: unverified) (one of `verified`, `unverified`) |

## Actions

Whether an action needs `sudo` is read from the rule the node enforces, with the other arguments left out (e.g. `node care` reads, `node care measure` needs `sudo`).

| Action | Needs `sudo` |
|---|---|
| `list` | no |
| `add-source` | yes |
| `add-catalog` | yes |
| `remove-source` | yes |
| `enable` | yes |
| `disable` | yes |
| `trust` | yes |
| `rename` | yes |
| `reconcile` | yes |
